Extract the richness and sampling fraction of clades from grafted phylogenies

Source: R/extract_sampling_info.R
extract_sampling_info.Rd

Summarize, in each grafted phylogeny, the species of each clade listed in total_richness_per_clades: species of the backbone, grafted species, and unsampled species (species of the clade that are neither in the backbone nor grafted). It then derives the sampling fraction of each clade that can be used in downstream analyses to account for the clade-specific sampling fractions (e.g., diversification models).

The function works a posteriori, on the output of phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() or phylograftR::graft_missing_clades() (a phylogeny, a set of simulations, or the list of maps obtained with a "multiSimmap"). The counts are taken in each grafted phylogeny. With graft_missing_taxa(), they can differ among simulations and maps, as a taxon can end up in different clades. With graft_missing_clades(), they are the same in all the phylogenies, as each missing clade is always grafted on the stem of its sister clade.

Usage

extract_sampling_info(phy_grafted, total_richness_per_clades)

Arguments

phy_grafted

A grafted phylogeny (class "phylo"), a set of grafted phylogenies (class "multiPhylo", e.g., several simulations), or a list of them with one element per map (output of the grafting functions with a "multiSimmap"). The phylogenies must have the elements $grafted_tips and $grafted_edges (see phylograftR::identify_grafted()).

total_richness_per_clades

A list with the total number of species of the clades, as used for the grafting. Items:

  • $Target_clade (clades defined for the taxa grafted with phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa()) or $Sister_clade (sister clades of the missing clades grafted with phylograftR::graft_missing_clades()). Exactly one of them must be provided. List of character vectors of tips of the backbone: a pair of tips defines the clade as their most recent common ancestor (MRCA), and a single tip defines a terminal branch. Node IDs are not accepted: convert them with phylograftR::convert_nodes_to_tips().

  • $Target_clade_name or $Sister_clade_name: (Optional) Character vector of the names of the clades, same length as the clades (NA if a clade has no name). The names must be unique. They are reported in the Clade_name column of the output.

  • $total_richness: Vector of positive integers, same length as the clades. Total number of species of each clade, i.e., backbone species, grafted species, and unsampled species. Use NA if unknown.

It can also be the list of both types of missing lineages as list(taxa = ..., clades = ...), as returned by phylograftR::build_total_richness_per_clades() and phylograftR::import_total_richness_per_clades() when both types are provided (e.g., to use with phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa_and_clades()).

Value

A data.frame, with one row per clade and phylogeny.

With a list(taxa, clades) covering both types of missing lineages, the output is a named list with the elements taxa and clades, each data.frame containing the following columns:

  • map Character string. Name of the stochastic map (NA if no map was used).

  • simulation Integer. Index of the simulation.

  • seed Integer. Seed of the simulation (NA if unknown).

  • Clade_name Character string. Name of the clade (NA if it has no name). Only if the names of the clades are provided in total_richness_per_clades.

  • Clade_tips Character string. Tips used to identify the clade.

  • total_richness Numeric. Total number of species of the clade: provided, or derived if NA was provided.

  • total_richness_provided Logical. Whether the total richness of the clade was provided.

  • nb_backbone_species Integer. Number of species of the clade that are in the backbone.

  • nb_grafted_species Integer. Number of species of the clade that were grafted.

  • nb_unsampled_species Numeric. Number of species of the clade that are neither in the backbone nor grafted. Negative (conflictual) if the clade has more species than expected.

  • sampling_fraction Numeric. Fraction of the clade richness present in the grafted phylogeny, (nb_backbone_species + nb_grafted_species) / total_richness.

Attributes: "type" ("taxa" if the clades are $Target_clade, "clades" if they are $Sister_clade).

Details

Species of a clade

The species of a clade are the tips that descend from its MRCA in the grafted phylogeny: the backbone species of the clade, and the grafted taxa that were grafted within it. It depends on the phylogeny, as a taxon grafted in a target clade can fall in a clade nested within it, and as the taxa grafted on the stem branch of a clade are sister to the clade, so they are not part of it. The exception is the clade of a single tip of $Target_clade: its terminal branch is its only branch, so the taxa grafted on it are part of the clade. For $Sister_clade, the missing clades are grafted on the stem branch of the sister clade and are never part of it.

Unsampled species and sampling fraction

For a clade with a total richness provided, nb_unsampled_species = total_richness - nb_backbone_species - nb_grafted_species. For a clade without a total richness (NA), the unsampled species are those identified in the largest clades nested within it that have a total richness (none if there is none), and its total richness is derived as nb_backbone_species + nb_grafted_species + nb_unsampled_species (it can differ among phylogenies). The sampling fraction is (nb_backbone_species + nb_grafted_species) / total_richness.

In problematic cases, the number of species of a clade can be higher than its total richness: for example, a taxon known to belong to a genus can be grafted in a subclade of this genus whose provided total richness did not include it. The number of unsampled species is then negative and the sampling fraction is higher than 1. These values are returned as they are, with a warning listing the clades and the number of phylogenies concerned, so the clades and the total richness provided can be reviewed. When a clade without a total richness is derived from nested clades, the negative values of the nested clades are counted as 0.

See also

Other functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() to graft taxa based on target clades and excluded subclades.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_clades() to graft groups of missing taxa as sister clades on backbone clades.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa_and_clades() to graft missing taxa and missing clades in one run, with a single set of inputs.

  • phylograftR::extract_grafting_info() to extract a posteriori information on the location of grafted lineages.

  • phylograftR::extract_BD_model_summary() to extract a posteriori information on the birth-death models fitted during grafting.

Author

Maël Doré

Examples

# --- Prepare data --- #

# Create a toy backbone phylogeny: ultrametric, with a root age of 50 time units
set.seed(1234)
phy <- ape::rcoal(n = 30)
phy$edge.length <- phy$edge.length / max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(phy)) * 50

# Two nested clades: B is nested within A
clade_A <- c("t26", "t18") # 17 backbone species
clade_B <- c("t26", "t3")  # 9 backbone species, nested within A

# List the missing taxa to graft: 3 taxa in clade A and 1 taxon in clade B
missing_taxa_list <- list(
  Taxon_name = c("X1", "X2", "X3", "X4"),
  Target_clade = list(X1 = clade_A, X2 = clade_A, X3 = clade_A, X4 = clade_B),
  # Optional names of the clades (one per taxon): they must match those of total_richness_per_clades
  Target_clade_name = c("clade_A", "clade_A", "clade_A", "clade_B"))

# Total richness of the target clades
# NA = unknown richness (i.e., no unsampled species beyond nested clades)
total_richness_per_clades <- list(
  Target_clade = list(clade_A, clade_B),
  Target_clade_name = c("clade_A", "clade_B"),
  total_richness = c(25, 12))

# --- Graft the taxa (several simulations) --- #

grafted_phys <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,
                                   total_richness_per_clades = total_richness_per_clades,
                                   nb_simulations = 5, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)

# --- Extract the sampling information --- #

sampling_info <- extract_sampling_info(phy_grafted = grafted_phys,
                                       total_richness_per_clades = total_richness_per_clades)
sampling_info[, c("simulation", "Clade_name", "nb_backbone_species", "nb_grafted_species",
                  "nb_unsampled_species", "sampling_fraction")]
#>    simulation Clade_name nb_backbone_species nb_grafted_species
#> 1           1    clade_A                  17                  4
#> 2           1    clade_B                   9                  3
#> 3           2    clade_A                  17                  4
#> 4           2    clade_B                   9                  1
#> 5           3    clade_A                  17                  4
#> 6           3    clade_B                   9                  2
#> 7           4    clade_A                  17                  4
#> 8           4    clade_B                   9                  1
#> 9           5    clade_A                  17                  4
#> 10          5    clade_B                   9                  3
#>    nb_unsampled_species sampling_fraction
#> 1                     4         0.8400000
#> 2                     0         1.0000000
#> 3                     4         0.8400000
#> 4                     2         0.8333333
#> 5                     4         0.8400000
#> 6                     1         0.9166667
#> 7                     4         0.8400000
#> 8                     2         0.8333333
#> 9                     4         0.8400000
#> 10                    0         1.0000000

# The sampling fraction of clade B varies among simulations:
# the taxa assigned to clade A can be grafted within clade B (nested in A, so they count for B)
# or in A outside of B. As such, the richness of B differs between grafted phylogenies,
# while all the taxa are always in A (constant sampling fraction).
tapply(X = sampling_info$sampling_fraction,
       INDEX = list(sampling_info$Clade_name, sampling_info$simulation),
       FUN = mean)
#>            1         2         3         4    5
#> clade_A 0.84 0.8400000 0.8400000 0.8400000 0.84
#> clade_B 1.00 0.8333333 0.9166667 0.8333333 1.00

# --- Both types of missing lineages, grafted in one run --- #

# With graft_missing_taxa_and_clades(), the totals of both types are provided as list(taxa, clades)
both_list <- list(
  taxa = missing_taxa_list,
  clades = list(Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2"), Sister_clade = list(M1 = clade_B, M2 = "t5")))
both_richness <- list(
  taxa = total_richness_per_clades,
  clades = list(Sister_clade = list(clade_B, "t5"), total_richness = c(12, 4)))

grafted_both <- graft_missing_taxa_and_clades(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = both_list,
                                              total_richness_per_clades = both_richness,
                                              nb_simulations = 3, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)

# Output: a named list with the table of each type
sampling_both <- extract_sampling_info(phy_grafted = grafted_both,
                                       total_richness_per_clades = both_richness)
names(sampling_both)
#> [1] "taxa"   "clades"
sampling_both$clades[, c("simulation", "Clade_tips", "nb_grafted_species", "sampling_fraction")]
#>   simulation Clade_tips nb_grafted_species sampling_fraction
#> 1          1    t26, t3                  3         1.0000000
#> 2          1         t5                  0         0.2500000
#> 3          2    t26, t3                  1         0.8333333
#> 4          2         t5                  0         0.2500000
#> 5          3    t26, t3                  2         0.9166667
#> 6          3         t5                  0         0.2500000
